html:
The Gold Coast Colony was the British colony on the coast of what is now Ghana, proclaimed in 1874. The map shows it in its 1880 snapshot, when it was still a strip along the sea; its later, larger form is told under Gold Coast.

Britain had long held forts on this coast among the Fante states. In 1872 it bought the Dutch forts, including Elmina. The Asante kingdom, which saw Elmina as its own outlet to the sea, invaded. In the 1873 and 1874 campaign of the Anglo-Ashanti wars, a British army burned the Asante capital Kumasi.

Britain then made the coast a crown colony, and in 1877 moved its capital from Cape Coast to Accra. Asante itself was annexed in 1901, and the colony grew into the country that became independent as Ghana in 1957.
